RED-FLAGS REPORT
Prairie Aerostructures Holdings — Diligence Review (Matter File 10)

Prepared for: Client Engagement Team
Operative record: Deal materials — diligence review; Counterparty markup; Schedules and exhibits; Deal correspondence (controlling latest partner instruction).

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION
The latest partner email controls over the superseded threads: the client will CONCEDE the indemnification basket conversion (from a deductible to a tipping basket), but treats ANY survival-period reduction for the core representations as a WALK-AWAY issue. All priorities below are assessed against this instruction.

SUMMARY
The counterparty markup (doc 36) and the disclosure schedules (doc 88) each qualify the base materials (doc 10). Reconciliation shows the counterparty's revision undercuts buyer protection in several material respects. One red flag — the survival-period reduction — is a client walk-away issue and must be treated as deal-critical. Two further flags (silent indemnification-cap reduction and MAE regulatory carve-outs that intersect disclosed pending inquiries) materially shift value. One item (basket conversion) is conceded and therefore is NOT flagged as an issue for the client, but should be documented as an explicit concession.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RED FLAG 1 — SURVIVAL-PERIOD REDUCTION (WALK-AWAY ISSUE) — CRITICAL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Source: Counterparty markup materially shortens survival for the core representations/warranties.

Analysis: The counterparty introduces "a new limitation period [that] shortens survival for the core representations." This directly contradicts Exhibit B, which "sets the survival matrix" for the deal. Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities whose enforceability depends on the survival window.

Controlling Instruction: Any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. The client will not accept a shortened survival window for the core reps.

Recommendation: Flag as deal-critical. Reject the reduced survival period and hold to the Exhibit B survival matrix for all core representations and warranty claims. Do not proceed on current markup terms without restoring the original survival periods. This is the single highest-priority red flag and should be raised with the client immediately.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RED FLAG 2 — SILENT INDEMNIFICATION-CAP REDUCTION — HIGH
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Source: Counterparty markup "silently reduces" the indemnification cap.

Analysis: The base materials contain negotiated indemnification provisions. The counterparty reduces the cap without disclosed justification. Plainly read with Schedule 5.2, which lists retained liabilities, the cap reduction would shift those retained liabilities onto the buyer / reduce recourse for indemnifiable losses.

Recommendation: Require the cap to be restored to the base-negotiated level, and confirm that the cap applies without the silent reduction. Reconcile Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities against the reduced cap so no liability is silently shifted to the buyer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RED FLAG 3 — MAE DEFINITION ADDING REGULATORY CARVE-OUTS (INTERSECTS SCHEDULE 3.7 PENDING INQUIRIES) — HIGH
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Source: Counterparty markup adds carve-outs to the Material Adverse Effect (MAE) definition "for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter." Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries.

Analysis: The carve-out is tailored to regulatory action of the exact kind at issue. When read against Schedule 3.7, which discloses two pending regulatory inquiries, the carve-out would operate to exclude precisely the regulatory exposure already disclosed — effectively gutting the buyer's MAE protection for the very risk identified in the data room. The scheduled exceptions control over general statements, so this carve-out must be read together with the Schedule 3.7 disclosures.

Recommendation: Flag the MAE carve-out as a material red flag. Either delete the tailored regulatory carve-out or carve back the exception so it does not swallow the disclosed Schedule 3.7 inquiries. Confirm the buyer retains MAE (and related closing/termination) protection for the disclosed regulatory matters.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ITEM 4 — BASKET CONVERSION TO TIPPING BASKET — CONCEDED (NOT A FLAG)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Source: Counterparty markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

Analysis: A tipping basket is, all else equal, generally less favorable to the buyer than a deductible. However, per the controlling partner instruction, the client has CONCEDED this point. It is therefore not a red flag for the client.

Recommendation: Document the concession explicitly so the record reflects client agreement. Proceed on the basket conversion as conceded, and do not re-litigate it.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECONCILIATION NOTE — SCHEDULED EXCEPTIONS CONTROL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Per the schedule/exhibits materials, the disclosure schedules (3.7, 5.2) and Exhibit B "control over general statements in the base diligence materials." Every red flag above was reconciled against the base materials, the counterparty markup, and the controlling schedule/exhibit source. Any inconsistency between the general base language and a scheduled exception or exhibit is resolved in favor of the schedule/exhibit.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
RECOMMENDED NEXT STEPS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Raise Red Flag 1 (survival-period reduction) to the client immediately as a walk-away issue; do not accept the shortened survival window for core reps.
2. Reject the silent indemnification-cap reduction and restore the base cap, reconciling Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.
3. Redline the MAE carve-out so it does not exempt the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7.
4. Confirm the basket-conversion concession is properly documented and reflected in the term sheet.
5. Hold the survival matrix to Exhibit B for all core representations.

END OF REPORT
